features.title: Store a Session's request-header tool catalog once
features.summary: Owned fork of the native JSONL session-persistence backend. Every request that begins a new message series appends a request/header event carrying the full assembled tool catalog — 455 tools, ~270 KB in one measured Session, byte-identical on 31 of 34 headers. This fork writes that catalog into the artifact once and stores a digest reference on every later request whose catalog matches, expanding the reference inline on read so every existing reader sees the same events. Logs written before this fork, and logs without a repeated catalog, read identically. The header line carries a marker, so a harness without this fork refuses the artifact instead of reading a reference as an empty tool list.

configuration.constraints: Absolute directory holding one directory per project and session; restated from the stock row because a patch replaces whole configs.
Physical encoding of one artifact: concatenated checksummed Zstandard frames, or plaintext JSONL. Dedupe applies to both.

failureModes: A reference whose catalog is absent from the artifact (a truncated or hand-edited log) refuses the read as corruption rather than returning a header without tools.
A harness without this fork rejects a marked artifact while parsing its header line: the marker is outside the closed header key set, so the log is never silently read as tool-less.
session-log export re-serializes from the read seam, so a downloaded archive is the canonical pre-fork v4 JSONL with every catalog inline: universally readable and larger than the stored artifact.
Every other behaviour is the pinned upstream code; drift is checked with scripts/native-fork-diff.mjs.

verification.testName: stores one catalog, reads it back for every series, and shrinks the artifact
reads a pre-fork log identically and refuses a pre-fork harness on a deduped one
dedupes inside compressed generations and across a reopened writer

verification.reason: Host-only storage fork with no surface of its own: it changes what one durable event row stores, and the Session conversation that shows those requests belongs to the chat plugin.

telemetry.reason: In-process artifact encoding under the persistence reads and writes the Host already performs: no network, socket, or job of its own.
